hook: Physicists at the University of Queensland just sent a binary message through a solid wall!

sections.voiceover: Physicists at the University of Queensland just sent a binary message through a solid wall!
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a heavy, industrial steel counterweight suspended in a shaft.

sections.voiceover: Can this 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight bypass brick walls that block traditional electromagnetic waves?
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing the Parnell Building exterior and a diagram of an elevator moving between two levels.

sections.voiceover: These gravitational pulses are unblockable, but the transmission requires nearly one hour to complete.
sections.visual_cue: Abstract representation of waves passing unimpeded through a dense brick wall.

sections.voiceover: Andrew J. Groszek and his team successfully transmitted the word gravity in binary code. The system achieved a transmission rate of 1 bit per minute using a sensitive gravimeter.
sections.visual_cue: Text overlay displaying the word 'GRAVITY' appearing one bit at a time in binary code.

sections.voiceover: It took nearly one hour for the 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight to complete that binary transmission.
sections.visual_cue: A digital timer counting up to sixty minutes in a laboratory setting.
